key_insight: ClinMM-Bench shows that multimodal clinical models can often suggest plausible diagnoses, but reliable multi-turn diagnostic reasoning remains inconsistent.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark better reflects real clinical workflow by testing how models update hypotheses as new multimodal information is revealed over time.
method: Built a multi-turn multimodal benchmark with 1,089 real-world cases and 3,760 images across eight specialties.
Evaluated 15 representative MLLMs using a two-level framework: diagnostic accuracy and reasoning quality.
Analyzed common failure modes including premature closure, visual hallucination, and information synthesis errors.
evidence_signal: Across 1,089 cases and 15 models, proprietary systems had the best overall accuracy, but fully correct diagnoses were still limited and reasoning quality remained weak.
watch_item: Benchmark results do not imply clinical readiness, since even strong models showed substantial reasoning failures and error modes that could affect safety in real use.
paper_title: Evaluating Multi-Turn Multimodal Diagnostic Reasoning on Challenging Real-World Clinical Cases
